claim: Bayern-Ticket 2026 costs €34 solo / €44 for 2 / €55 for 3 / €64 for 4 / €74 for 5, second class, with unlimited regional and S-Bahn travel on weekdays from 09:00 till 03:00 next morning, midnight on weekends/holidays.
quote: €34 for a solo traveller or €44 for 2 people travelling together, €55 for 3 people, €64 for 4 people or €74 for 5 people... valid from 9:00 am until 3:00 am the following morning. On weekends and public holidays, validity starts at midnight.

claim: The official Deutsche Bahn Regional Day Ticket for Bavaria covers regional trains, S-Bahn, U-Bahn, trams and most buses across all of Bavaria for a single calendar day.
quote: Regional day ticket for Bavaria — unlimited travel on regional and S-Bahn trains, U-Bahn metro trains, most buses, and trams throughout Bavaria.

claim: Munich → Füssen is ~2h10 by regional train, then ~8 min on bus 73/78 to Hohenschwangau, putting the Ticketcenter within the 2-hour-each-way weekend window if you accept the bus add-on.
quote: Approximately 2 hours 10 minutes by train from Munich to Füssen, plus 8 minutes by bus to Hohenschwangau village.

claim: Neuschwanstein + Hohenschwangau combo ticket (the 'King's Ticket') runs about €31.50 adult in 2026 and must be booked roughly 3–4 weeks ahead because slots sell out.
quote: A Neuschwanstein + Hohenschwangau combo (King's Ticket) costs ~€31.50 adult in 2026... Book your castle tickets 3–4 weeks ahead, grab a Bayernticket at Munich HBF, aim for the 7:08 train.

claim: Common visitor complaint pattern: Neuschwanstein interior underwhelms because guided tours are limited to a few rooms with strict time constraints, while crowds and commercialization dominate the surrounding area — Hohenschwangau, Linderhof and the Marienbrücke viewpoint are recommended alternatives.
quote: the interior often underwhelms visitors, as tours are guided and limited to a few rooms with strict time constraints... Linderhof Palace — characterized as offering an 'intimate, beautifully preserved, peaceful' experience with low crowds.

claim: The official Dachau Memorial directions confirm S2 from Munich Hbf to Dachau Bahnhof, then bus 726 (direction Saubachsiedlung) to the KZ-Gedenkstätte stop, with admission to the memorial site free of charge.
quote: From Munich main station (Hauptbahnhof) take the S 2 (direction: Petershausen) to Dachau station. From there take the bus 726 (direction Saubachsiedlung) to the stop 'KZ-Gedenkstätte'.

claim: Dachau is the easiest half-day from Munich: S2 ~25 min, bus 726 ~10 min, free entry, with 2.5–3 hours minimum needed on-site to do the memorial justice — leaves the afternoon free for the city.
quote: The train ride takes approximately 25 minutes from Munich's Central Station... Bus 726... about 10 minutes... admission is free, and 2.5–3 hours is the minimum needed to do it justice.

claim: Kloster Andechs is reachable by S8 to Herrsching (~55 min from Munich Hbf) then a ~4 km forest walk through the Kiental or a short shuttle bus, making it a low-effort half-day for monastery + brewery + beer garden.
quote: Take the S8 train to Herrsching. This takes approximately 1 hour from Munich. From Herrsching, you have options: Either catch a bus to the monastery or hike through the Kiental valley up to the complex (around 4km).

claim: Official Munich tourism confirms Andechs as a monastery and brewery destination with Bräustüberl beer hall open 10:00–20:00, framed by city tourism as a classic Bavarian half-day combining baroque church, beer and Schweinshaxe.
quote: The Bräustüberl Biergarten is open year round from 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM... fabulous Rococo-Baroque church built in 1712, resting atop Heiliger Hill.

claim: Garmisch-Partenkirchen is ~80 min from Munich on the Bayerische Oberlandbahn; from there the Eibsee Seilbahn cable car reaches the Zugspitze summit in 10 minutes or the historic cogwheel train in ~75 minutes.
quote: Garmisch-Partenkirchen main station, reachable by train from Munich in about 80 minutes... direct Eibsee Seilbahn cable car takes 10 minutes... historic cogwheel train takes 75 minutes.

claim: Round-trip adult Zugspitze cable car on the Bavarian side is €62 in 2026, plan 3–4 hours at the summit, and arrive at the valley station before 09:00 on summer weekends to beat queues — making it a full-day burner.
quote: The Zugspitze cable car ticket costs €62 for an adult round-trip on the Bavarian side in 2026... Allow 3–4 hours for the full summit visit... Aim to arrive at the valley station before 9 AM.

claim: Munich Hbf to Salzburg Hbf runs hourly on ÖBB Railjet in 1h30 (regional in ~1h45–2h); the Bayern-Ticket exceptionally covers Salzburg even though it's in Austria, making a group day return ~€34–€74 instead of €60–80 on a Railjet.
quote: An express train links Munich & Salzburg every hour in each direction, taking as little as 1h30 for an Austrian railjet... a Bayern Ticket costs €34 for the first traveller plus around €10 for each additional traveller... even covers a same-day round trip from Munich to Salzburg.

claim: Berchtesgaden is the longest stretch in the feasible set: ~2h15 train via Freilassing change, then bus 841/843 to Königssee — official Munich tourism treats it as a day trip but warns it eats the entire day.
quote: Berchtesgaden: Tips for a day trip from Munich... the fastest trains from Munich to Berchtesgaden take around 2 hours and 16 minutes... usually need to make around 1 change during the journey, typically at Freilassing.

claim: Munich to Königssee end-to-end runs roughly 3.5 hours each way by train+bus versus ~2 hours by car, so Königssee on a 2-night weekend means accepting that day disappears entirely.
quote: From Munich to Königssee you'll spend about 2 hours by car or 3.5 hours by train and bus going in each direction.

claim: Tegernsee is reached by BOB (Bayerische Regiobahn) from Munich Hbf's Starnberger Flügelbahnhof in ~1h05, leaving from platforms 33/34 — short enough for a half-day or a relaxed full day at the Alpine lake.
quote: BOB trains from Munich's main train station (HBF) to Tegernsee... platforms 33/34 from the Starnberg Wing... around 1 hour 8 minutes.

claim: The BOB splits at Schaftlach into Tegernsee/Lenggries cars and at Holzkirchen for Schliersee/Bayrischzell, so travellers must board the correctly labelled carriage or end up at the wrong lake.
quote: The train splits at 'Schaftlach' station with one part continuing to Lenggries and the other to Tegernsee, with each car's destination clearly indicated.

claim: Linderhof requires Munich → Murnau → Oberammergau by train (~1h50) then bus 9622 to the palace, total ~3 hours each way — beyond the strict 2-hour rule, so it only fits a weekend if paired with Neuschwanstein on an organised tour or done by car (1h30 via A95).
quote: leave Munich on the 8:32 RB (direction Innsbruck), get off at Murnau at 9:27 and catch the 9:42 RB to Oberammergau... 11:25 bus to Linderhof, arriving at 11:58... By car, it takes approximately 1.5 hours via the A95 motorway.
